source.title: Continual Learning via Sparse Memory Finetuning

assessments.primary_source_quality: Strong current primary preprint from Meta FAIR/UC Berkeley with a purpose-built memory-layer language model, matched new-knowledge acquisition, dense full-finetuning and LoRA baselines, held-out forgetting probes, and two continual-QA settings. It is not peer reviewed in the evidence inspected here, is centered on a 1.3B memory-layer model, and no independent replication was identified.
assessments.quantitative_result: On a stream of TriviaQA facts with matched acquisition of the new knowledge, the primary abstract reports NaturalQuestions F1 degradation of 89% under full finetuning, 71% under LoRA, and only 11% under sparse memory finetuning. A streamed-document SimpleQA setting shows the same qualitative stability/plasticity advantage, with forgetting also probed on NaturalQuestions/GSM8K.
assessments.matched_baseline: Good. The comparison explicitly holds new-knowledge acquisition approximately matched while comparing full dense updates, LoRA and sparse slot-localized updates. Remaining differences include the specialized memory-layer architecture and the fact that sparse slot selection and sparse parameterization are jointly involved.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Moderately strong for the native claim that localizing plasticity to selectively accessed memory slots can reduce forgetting relative to full/LoRA updates in this architecture. The available evidence does not isolate every design choice or compare directly against frozen-base external retrieval at equal inference/storage cost.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Primary paper and author material expose the method and reported evaluations; no independently executed artifact reproduction was performed by this comparator and no external replication was located.
assessments.failure_evidence: Direct evidence that even parameter-efficient LoRA updates can retain substantial forgetting when plasticity still touches broadly shared paths, whereas slot-localized updates preserve old QA performance far better in the tested setup.
scope_limits: Specialized 1.3B memory-layer LM rather than a general arbitrary pretrained LLM.
Two QA continual-learning settings; not an autonomous-agent long-horizon task benchmark.
The 89%/71%/11% forgetting comparison should not be generalized beyond the matched acquisition and evaluation conditions used in the paper.
No direct comparison to external non-parametric retrieval under matched memory, latency and knowledge-acquisition constraints was identified.
This is evidence for localized parametric plasticity, not evidence that O currently needs parametric learning.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B/B+ for sparse memory-slot finetuning as a forgetting-reduction mechanism in the tested memory-layer LM and QA streams.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C at most for O or an O-adjacent learner until persistent parametric updating is itself justified and sparse-memory updates are compared with simpler frozen-base external-memory/context alternatives on matched downstream outcomes.

source.title: Continual Reinforcement Learning by Planning with Online World Models

assessments.primary_source_quality: High. This is a peer-reviewed ICML 2025 paper with an explicit Follow-The-Leader shallow online dynamics model, model-predictive-control planner, formal regret analysis, a six-task Continual Bench environment, same-model-planning-framework baselines, and an open implementation. The benchmark is introduced by the same work and no independent external replication was located.
assessments.quantitative_result: The worker's primary-table extraction reports model-based final average performance/regret (%): fine-tuning 24.86/37.74, SI 39.96/33.57, Coreset 61.83/30.83, Perfect Memory 73.09/30.95, and Online Agent 72.93/27.62. OA therefore nearly matches Perfect Memory average performance while achieving lower regret without an unbounded replay buffer. The primary PMLR page confirms the core architecture, same-framework comparisons, incremental updates and regret bound O(sqrt(K^2 D log T)); the study reports repeated-run aggregate evaluation.
assessments.matched_baseline: Strong within the benchmark. Fine-tuning, SI, Coreset, Perfect Memory and OA are compared under the same broad model-based planning framework. The key assumption is unusually favorable to the architecture: tasks share state space/dynamics and differ in reward functions, so a reward-agnostic dynamics model can be reused by construction.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Moderately strong for separating shared dynamics learning from task-specific reward adaptation and solving tasks through planning in this CRL class. The result does not establish that a world-model/planner architecture dominates policy adaptation when dynamics themselves shift, observations are very high-dimensional, or rewards/tasks cannot be cleanly separated.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Strong: peer-reviewed PMLR paper and public ContinualBench implementation. This comparator verified the primary PMLR record and method; the raw PDF endpoint could not be rendered through the browsing tool in this pass, so the exact table values remain tied to the already primary-verified worker extraction rather than a new PDF screenshot verification here.
assessments.external_replication: No independent replication located. The formal guarantee and several strong baseline families provide robustness within the paper, but not independent confirmation.
assessments.failure_evidence: Supports a concrete alternative to continually rewriting task-specific behavior: when tasks share dynamics, repeated policy updates/replay can be unnecessary and susceptible to forgetting, whereas a stable task-agnostic world model plus current-reward planning can preserve prior skills by construction under the model assumptions.
scope_limits: Six-task Continual Bench introduced by the same work.
Tasks share dynamics/state space and mainly differ in reward; this is a narrower setting than general continual learning.
The shallow model/planning formulation has moderate-dimensional state-space limitations noted by the paper.
The no-forgetting property is architectural under stated assumptions and should not be generalized to changing dynamics or arbitrary LLM knowledge adaptation.
A world-model architecture is not automatically appropriate for O unless a stable shared-dynamics abstraction and useful planning interface can be operationally demonstrated.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B+ approaching A- for the online-world-model + MPC mechanism within the paper's shared-dynamics continual-RL setting, supported by peer review, formal analysis, matched baselines and open code but lacking independent replication.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C/C+ until an O-relevant task family with stable reusable dynamics is defined and the architecture is compared against existing context/external-memory/action-selection approaches on matched held-out outcomes and cost.

cross_source_synthesis: Both candidates localize plasticity rather than continually rewriting broad shared behavior: sparse memory finetuning localizes parameter updates, while the Online Agent localizes continual change to a reusable dynamics model and leaves task adaptation to planning.

The world-model result has stronger source maturity and reproducibility because it is peer-reviewed and has open code, but its assumptions are narrower. Sparse memory finetuning shows a striking matched forgetting reduction but remains a recent specialized-architecture preprint.

Neither source is evidence that O should add parametric continual learning. Their strongest transferable contribution is the experimental principle that the component being made plastic should be explicitly localized and compared with simpler frozen/shared alternatives under interference tests.
